questions.question: What property do you use to enable CSS Grid on a container?
options: grid: enabled;
display: grid;
layout: grid;
grid-container: true;
questions.explanation: You enable CSS Grid by setting 'display: grid;' on the parent container. This makes the container a grid container and its children grid items.

questions.question: What is the main difference between Flexbox and CSS Grid?
options: Grid is one-dimensional, Flexbox is two-dimensional
Grid creates two-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns), while Flexbox is one-dimensional
There is no difference
Grid only works on mobile devices
questions.explanation: CSS Grid creates two-dimensional layouts (rows AND columns) with precise control, while Flexbox is one-dimensional (either row or column).

questions.question: What does 'grid-template-columns' do?
options: Defines how many rows the grid has
Defines how many columns the grid has and their sizes
Defines the gap between grid items
Defines the alignment of grid items
questions.explanation: 'grid-template-columns' defines how many columns your grid has and their sizes. For example, 'grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr;' creates three equal columns.

options: Three equal-width columns that automatically adjust to container size
Three fixed-width columns of 1 pixel each
One column that takes up 1/3 of the space
Three rows
questions.explanation: '1fr 1fr 1fr' creates three equal-width columns using fractional units. The 'fr' units automatically adjust to fit the container size, so each column gets an equal share of the available space.

questions.question: What does 'grid-column: span 2;' do?
options: Makes an item span across 2 rows
Makes an item span across 2 columns
Creates a 2-column gap
Moves an item 2 columns to the right
questions.explanation: 'grid-column: span 2;' makes an item span across 2 columns. The item will take up the space of two columns in the grid.

questions.question: What does 'grid-row: span 2;' do?
options: Makes an item span across 2 columns
Makes an item span across 2 rows
Creates a 2-row gap
Moves an item 2 rows down
questions.explanation: 'grid-row: span 2;' makes an item span across 2 rows. The item will take up the space of two rows in the grid, making it taller.

options: The item spans from column 1 to column 3 (spans 2 columns)
The item is in column 1 and has a width of 3
The item moves 1 column and spans 3
The item is positioned at coordinates 1, 3
questions.explanation: 'grid-column: 1 / 3;' means the item starts at column 1 and ends at column 3, which means it spans 2 columns. This is an alternative syntax to 'grid-column: span 2;'.

options: Three equal columns
First column fixed at 200px, other two columns flexible and equal
Three fixed columns of 200px each
Two columns, one 200px and one flexible
questions.explanation: This creates a grid where the first column is fixed at 200 pixels, and the remaining two columns are flexible (1fr each) and will split the remaining available space equally.

options: An item that spans 2 columns and 2 rows, creating a large featured area
An item that is 2 pixels wide and 2 pixels tall
An item with 2px margins
An item positioned at column 2, row 2
questions.explanation: This makes the item span 2 columns horizontally and 2 rows vertically, creating a large featured area that takes up 4 grid cells (2×2).

questions.question: What does 'repeat(3, 1fr)' in 'grid-template-columns' create?
options: Three equal columns (shorthand for 1fr 1fr 1fr)
Three rows
A gap of 3fr between columns
Three fixed-width columns
questions.explanation: 'repeat(3, 1fr)' is shorthand that creates three equal columns, equivalent to writing '1fr 1fr 1fr'. It's useful for creating multiple columns of the same size.

options: A card grid
A sidebar layout with a 200px width sidebar and flexible content area
A three-column layout
A centered content area
questions.explanation: This creates a sidebar layout where the first column is fixed at 200px (the sidebar) and the second column is flexible (1fr), taking up the remaining space for the main content.

options: A fixed 3-column grid
As many columns as fit (minimum 250px each), automatically responsive
A single column layout
A grid with 250px gaps
questions.explanation: This creates a responsive card grid that automatically creates as many columns as can fit, with each column being at least 250px wide. It's perfect for responsive designs that adapt to different screen sizes.
